Thanks — looping in my legal playbook responses and clarifying commitments from Redwood Legal:

1) Owner commitments
- I will be primary SME for all substantive legal items (indemnity, liability caps, data residency, breach notification, export controls).
- Jordan will own privacy / DPA technical language and scope. Ben will triage commercial/SLA items and run delivery impact analysis.

2) Turnaround SLAs (Redwood Legal commitments)
- Triage & acknowledgement on receipt: within 8 business hours of upload to the queue.
- Non-substantive edits: 24–48 hours reply with tracked changes.
- Substantive items: initial position within 72 hours; if additional redlines required, target consolidated language within 5 business days.
- If Acme identifies > 3 high-severity items at once, we’ll request a quick sync (30–45m) to triage and avoid circular redlining.

3) Escalation path
- If either party needs an exception to the above timing, escalate to me and Ben and we’ll determine whether an expedited review is required.

4) Dependencies / blockers we flagged (from Redwood side)
- Data residency: we need the specific region and retention needs to evaluate feasible commitments (e.g., EU-only, US-only, hybrid).
- SLA credits: if the ask moves to per-month penalty credits that materially increase cost, we’ll need product/ops sign-off; Ben will own that coordination.

I’ll post a filled example row in the Redline_Queue_Template with a sample substantive item so Acme can confirm the level of detail you expect.
